proof.criterion: Acceptance 3: the cause is named with evidence, and for a product race the code handles it.
proof.surface: The internal/bus test binary against a real in-process three-server nats-server v2.10.29 cluster, the server CI pins.
proof.command: In a scratch copy of packages/envoy at base 8a911ecc, with temporary instrumentation at all four refusal sites: a probe sending one stream update from three clients at once, 300 rounds (900 requests), `go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestProbeConcurrentUpdatesOfOneStream$' ./internal/bus/`; plus `go test -count=50` and `-count=150` of 'TestTwoStartsRaisingOneStreamAtOnceBothSucceed$' and a 30-run of the same body with eight starts.
proof.observed: The probe caught the refusal in 6.6 s: `UpdateStream refused: err="nats: subjects overlap with an existing stream" http=400 code=10065`, 1 of 900 requests. The acceptance test itself failed 0 of 200 iterations and the eight-start variant 0 of 30 (240 starts), with no create-branch line at all, so `StreamInfo` never answered `stream not found` for the stream that existed and `AddStream` was never refused. The refused call is UpdateStream; nats-server before v2.12.5 skips a stream from its overlap check by pointer identity (jsClusteredStreamUpdateRequest and subjectsOverlap, v2.10.29 server/jetstream_cluster.go:6280 and :560-576), so an update landing in between leaves the stream overlapping itself.
proof.headSha: 8a911ecca3a5 (the base; the trace is of the unfixed code)
proof.negativeControl: The same probe against three real nats-server v2.15.1 binaries, which carry the upstream fix cb1afd68d014: 0 refusals in 900 requests, so the refusal is that server bug and not a property of concurrent updates.

trickyParts: The plan's section 1 hypothesis (a refused AddStream after a clustered StreamInfo answered stream not found) is not what happens: 240 starts produced no create-branch entry at all. The architect's decision 6 covered this case, and the create paths in stream.go and kv.go are left exactly as they were, with plan sections 2 and 3 dropped.

updateStream re-sends the caller's own configuration, which is the write a server without the race would have taken after the other update; it re-sends only while the stream, read again, does not already hold what the caller asked for, so it never overwrites a concurrent write that already satisfied this caller.

The acceptance-5 filter keeps a record with no name attribute on purpose: the expected record of TestADrainEndsTheKVWatchersBeforeTheConnection/consumer_already_gone comes from kvwatch, which logs no client name. A client started without WithName also passes that way, which the helper's comment says.
nats.go names no constant for error code 10065; the package's own jsStreamStoreFailed in nats.go is the house precedent for declaring one beside its user.
deviations: Plan sections 2, 3 and 4 (the create-path re-read in ensureStreamWithConfig and EnsureKeyValue, and their three injected tests) are not implemented: the instrumented runs showed no refusal and no not-found answer on that path in 240 starts, and the INFRA-14 architect decided on that trace to fix updateStream instead and to keep no create-path handling.

Plan section 5a's per-client WithName instrumentation of every cluster test was not needed: the base acceptance-5 run printing every captured record names the leaking client by its three server URLs against the test's one, which is what 5a asked for. Section 5b is implemented as written.
Plan section 6's one-off ran in byte-identical copies of the base and head trees under $TMPDIR (diff -r clean) rather than in the workspace, so no throwaway file ever entered the workspace.

Acceptance 1's base measurement is an escape-clause case in this pod: 0 of 200 iterations failed here, against the planner's 1 of 50 at the same commit and CI run 40857522211. The pull request quotes all three, and the change's failing-first proof is the concurrent-update measurement, which fails 4 of 5 runs at the base in seconds.
discoveredComplexity: The hub's nats-server v2.15.1 does not have this race: 0 refusals in 900 concurrent updates, because v2.12.5 shipped cb1afd68d014. The failure is CI's pinned v2.10.29 and any deployment on a server older than v2.12.5.
